claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys are governed by nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneity modulates the sharpness and reversibility of the first-order magnetostructural transition through local variations in magnetic and structural coupling.
The as-deposited alloy has a single-phase hexagonal structure.
Moderate-temperature annealing can introduce nanoscale compositional heterogeneity through partial phase separation or clustering.
The proposed annealing temperature is between 0.4 and 0.6 of the alloy's absolute melting temperature.
Annealing in the proposed range can generate nanoscale heterogeneity without producing macroscopic secondary phases.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneity produces local variations in magnetic and structural coupling.
Compositionally heterogeneous regions have different local transition temperatures.
A distribution of local transition temperatures broadens the magnetostructural transition.
A broadened transition enables a more gradual and reversible phase transformation under low applied magnetic fields.
Compared with the as-deposited baseline, the annealed alloy will have a broader magnetocaloric response.
Compared with the as-deposited baseline, the annealed alloy will have a reduced peak entropy change.
Compared with the as-deposited baseline, the annealed alloy will have significantly lower hysteresis losses during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The as-deposited baseline has a sharp, hysteretic magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
The predictions apply only while heterogeneity remains nanoscale, macroscopic secondary phases do not form, and mechanical stability is retained.
